messages:
jamie: Quick design check — proposing a 'sparse-mirror' prefetch API to help offload-heavy embeddings workloads. Sketch below, want feedback on interface + failure modes. :thinking:

alex: TL;DR? How does this differ from existing prefetch hints + KV cache?

jamie: It's for backing host pages: create lightweight read-only mirrors of hot subranges so inference can avoid page faults when offloaded. Not full staging, just pinned mirrored ranges + async refresh.

maria: Interesting. Do we keep mirrors tenant-local? How do we evict when memory pressure?

jamie: Mirrors are tenant-local, accounted to tenant quota. Eviction uses soft-lease like existing host staging but with lower residency cost hint. Evict order: mirrors -> staging -> resident.

kyle: What about correctness if model writes back (rare) — we treat mirrors as immutable snapshots, rebuild on mutation with write-through mark.

alex: Can you paste the API sketch?

jamie: ```json
{
  "prefetch": "sparse-mirror",
  "ranges": [[offset, length], ...],
  "priority": "low|med|high",
  "ttl_ms": 300000
}
```

maria: TTL seems fine. Need metrics: mirror_hits, mirror_misses, rebuilds, memory_bytes.

ops-bot: deploy-probe: Prefetch controller running in canary on pool-a.

kyle: Failure modes: if mirror rebuilds thrash under write storms, we should backoff per-range and demote to staging.

jamie: Agreed. Backoff proposal: exponential per-range with jitter, signal to planner to drop further mirrors for tenant for 1s.

alex: How does routing pick mirror vs resident model variant? We don't change routing. Mirror is transparent to runtime via page-fault bypass path.

maria: Also need to consider NUMA locality — when mirror created, prefer host memory local to serving CPU of the slot.

jamie: yep add "preferred_numa": int optional in request.

kyle: Security: ensure KMS/HSM not exposed via mirror metadata, and audit log each mirror creation.

jamie: Plan: implement controller + tiny per-range state machine, add telemetry, run canary, measure tail-latency reduction on embed-heavy workloads. Any objections?

alex: No objections, but add charging model — count mirror bytes in tenant usage.

maria: +1. Can we prototype with a small in-memory slab to validate? I can take a spike.

jamie: Awesome — assigning spike to @maria. I'll open RFC PR with design + state diagrams.

kyle: One more: include a 'force-refresh' admin op to flush snapshot for debugging.

jamie: good call.

maria: I'll drop a rough perf goal: 90th p95 token latency reduction by 20% for kg/embedding batch 1.

alex: cool. follow-up in #design-docs when PR ready :thumbsup:
